question: How do you express, train and monitor logistic regression and a feed-forward network on MNIST with TensorFlow's graph, variable, session and device primitives?
contributions: Introduces TensorFlow variables, operations, placeholders, sessions, variable scopes and device placement
Builds and trains a logistic regression MNIST model and a two-hidden-layer ReLU network, with TensorBoard logging

results.claim: Logistic regression on MNIST reaches 91.9% test accuracy.
results.setup: MNIST 28x28, 784-10 softmax, plain SGD lr 0.01, batch 100, script sets training_epochs=1000 but text says 100 epochs
results.quote: Running the script gives us a final accuracy of 91.9% on the test set within 100 epochs
results.note: Script sets training_epochs = 1000; prose says 100 epochs. Elsewhere the same model is called an 8.1% error rate.

results.claim: Feed-forward net with two 256-unit ReLU hidden layers reaches 98.2% accuracy on MNIST.
results.setup: MNIST, 784-256-256-10, He-style normal init stddev sqrt(2/n_in), softmax folded into loss, 300 epochs; split (test vs validation) and lr/batch not restated for this run
results.quote: The model operates with an accuracy of 98.2%, which is nearly a 78% reduction in the per-digit error rate compared to our first attempt.
results.note: Summary says 1.8 errors per 100 digits. (8.1-1.8)/8.1 = 77.8%, consistent with the 78% claim.

results.claim: Logistic regression error rate on MNIST is 8.1%, which the authors say would mean errors on nearly 30% of 4-digit check amounts.
results.setup: Logistic regression MNIST model; 4-digit amounts treated as 4 independent digit reads
results.quote: Using  a logistic regression model, we were able to achieve an 8.1% error rate on the MNIST dataset.

results.claim: He et al. (2015) show weight variance for ReLU units should be 2/n_in; the chapter says switching back to uniform(-1,1) init significantly hurts the ReLU net, with no number given.
results.source: He et al. 2015, Delving Deep into Rectifiers
results.note: No measured effect size is reported.

limits: Teaches TensorFlow 1.x graph/session API (tf.Session, placeholder, feed_dict, tf.initialize_all_variables, tf.mul, tf.scalar_summary, tf.merge_all_summaries, tf.train.SummaryWriter(graph_def=), softmax_cross_entropy_with_logits(output,y) positional logits-first, Python 2 print statements, pip tensorflow 'for Python 2.7', CUDA 8.0 / cuDNN manual install); all removed or renamed in TF 2.x, so code does not run as printed.

Code has errors: inference() in logistic example creates constant_initializer but never assigns it to init; install test uses tf.mul and defines a twice with b missing (prints 6); CUDA Toolkit 8.0 then 7.0 inconsistently; 'from read_data import get_minibatch()' is invalid syntax; mnist object never loaded in the script.
Reports single runs, no seeds, no variance; lr 0.01 and batch 100 given only for logistic regression; the multilayer run's lr/batch are not stated.
Chapter does not print authors or year in this extract; Theano vs Torch vs TensorFlow comparison reflects 2015-2017 state.
practices: Use tf.get_variable inside tf.variable_scope instead of tf.Variable when a sub-network is reused, so weights are shared rather than duplicated (p.49-50).
Call scope.reuse_variables() explicitly to enable sharing; default is to raise an over-sharing ValueError (p.50).
Split a model into inference, loss, training and evaluate functions (p.53-55).
Fold softmax into the loss (softmax_cross_entropy_with_logits) rather than the inference phase for better performance (p.61).
For ReLU layers initialise weights with normal stddev sqrt(2/fan_in) (p.60-61).
Pass an absolute path to tensorboard --logdir (p.58).
Use allow_soft_placement with tf.device so ops fall back when the chosen device is missing (p.51).
Log scalar cost per minibatch and validation error per epoch, and checkpoint with tf.train.Saver (default keeps latest five) (p.55-57).

 b = tf.get_variable("b", bias_shape, initializer=bias_init)
 return tf.matmul(input, W) + b
